sourceEvidence.label: IMS Voice Agent deployment and service source

assessment.summary: The lab needs one owned boundary for media authority, personal-data minimization, service identity, bounded retention, and horizontally consistent call state.

nonNegotiables: Preserve verified IMS subscriber calls and fail-open RTP behavior.
Keep mutable local topology in lab.env and credentials outside Git.
assumptions: No measured production load, latency, availability, tenancy, jurisdiction, or retention requirement was supplied.
Docker Compose remains the local development environment.

opportunities.title: Separate scalable media authority and personal-data boundaries
opportunities.summary: Remove ambient internal authority now, then move production replicas to workload identity and a durable call-state owner.
opportunities.diagnosis: The source showed a broad service network, unauthenticated control APIs, SDP-derived media authority, excessive secret exposure, unbounded process-local state, and analytics fields that were not required.

evidence.claim: Custom services shared a broad network and lacked consistent least-privilege, resource, and secret-distribution controls.
SIP AS passed an SDP-derived endpoint to an unauthenticated agent control API.
Voice Agent call state and event retention were process-local and its API accepted control without authentication.
Media Adapter needs raw packet observation and accepted unused SIP identity fields.
AI ingestion and event retrieval were unauthenticated and retained in process memory.
No production concurrency, regional, tenancy, retention, or availability contract exists yet, so cluster sizing and technology selection remain unknown.

desiredInvariants: Only authenticated service workloads can mutate agent call state.
Agent RTP destinations are restricted to the configured RTPengine and allocated port range.
Subscriber credentials and identifiers are visible only to components with a declared need.
Audio is transient by default and metadata retention is bounded by purpose and TTL.
Every horizontal replica observes a consistent call-state owner or deterministic dialog affinity.

options.title: Hardened Compose boundary
options.summary: Authenticate local control, validate RTP authority, minimize data, bound resources, and reduce container privileges without changing the verified call flow.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Least privilege and runtime limits reduce the shared-host blast radius.
Authenticated control and exact RTPengine validation remove the observed ambient authority.
Authentication and bounds are added, but state remains local.
NET_RAW is retained only where required and identity fields are removed.
AI API authentication and bounded retention are implemented.
Production requirements still need owner decisions.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removes unauthenticated call control, arbitrary media destinations, and excessive custom-service privilege; shared host and token remain.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run verify-security.sh and targeted unauthorized/unanchored-media cases.

tradeoffs.assessment: Constant-time token checks and bounds add no external hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare call setup p95 and RTP packet counters before and after under the same call workload.

tradeoffs.assessment: Events, calls, logs, PIDs and container memory are bounded.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Drive maximum configured calls/events and inspect RSS plus rejection behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: Bounded overload and stale-call expiry improve recovery, while single-host failure remains.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Kill custom services independently and rerun fail-open and cleanup gates.

tradeoffs.assessment: Token volume lifecycle and read-only debugging require explicit procedures.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise clean start, token regeneration, log collection and rollback.

tradeoffs.assessment: The implementation preserved all live Phase 4B-4E gates.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Keep all gates in start-lab.ps1 and CI.

residualRisks: Shared bearer among authorized custom services

migrationNotes: Control APIs intentionally require authentication after deployment.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert the hardening commit; preserve database volumes; optionally remove the generated control-token volume.

options.title: Orchestrated shared service with durable call state
options.summary: Use workload identity, dialog-affine AS replicas, a durable state owner, RTPengine shards, bounded metadata queues, and independently autoscaled AI workers.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Workload policy and isolated roles replace broad local authority; Compose controls remain developer baseline.
mTLS policy and durable call control own media authorization.
Call state becomes consistent and recoverable across replicas.
Capture workers remain privileged but can be isolated per RTP shard.
A bounded TTL queue and workload identity control AI ingestion.
Technology and capacity depend on unsupplied production requirements.

tradeoffs.assessment: Per-workload identity and central call policy narrow authority and enable revocation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test workload impersonation, policy denial, key rotation and cross-namespace access.

tradeoffs.assessment: Durable state and queue operations add hops but permit independent scaling.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark p95/p99 setup and AI latency at target calls/s and RTP PPS.

tradeoffs.assessment: State replicas, queues and caches consume additional bounded memory.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure per-call state and queue depth during burst and recovery workloads.

tradeoffs.assessment: Node failures are containable, but state/queue availability becomes a new dependency for new calls.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run node, state, queue and region fault injection with drain/replay checks.

tradeoffs.assessment: PKI, state, queue, autoscaling and regional routing add operational burden.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Complete rotation, backup/restore, incident and regional failover rehearsals.

tradeoffs.assessment: Requires explicit state-machine, affinity and dual-run migration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Mirror state, replay histories, canary new calls and drain old dialogs before cutover.

migrationNotes: Introduce state ownership before adding replicas.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Route new calls to the prior single owner and drain candidate dialogs; retain mirrored state for audit.

options.title: Tenant-isolated service cells
options.summary: Deploy separate AS, media, agent, data, and key domains per tenant behind a tenant-aware IMS edge.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Dedicated cells contain tenant blast radius.
Media authority is scoped inside a tenant cell.
Call state and keys are tenant-local.
Raw capture remains privileged but tenant-scoped.
AI data and retention are tenant-specific.
Tenant obligations have not been supplied.

tradeoffs.assessment: Dedicated compute, key and data domains strongly reduce cross-tenant blast radius.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Attempt cross-cell network, identity, storage, backup and key access.

tradeoffs.assessment: Dedicated capacity reduces noisy neighbors but may strand resources.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark small and large tenant cells under burst and steady workloads.

tradeoffs.assessment: Service and cache overhead repeats per tenant.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure minimum viable cell footprint and idle-to-peak utilization.

tradeoffs.assessment: Tenant failures are isolated, while shared ingress and fleet orchestration remain common risks.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fail individual cells and shared routing separately.

tradeoffs.assessment: Fleet count, upgrades, backups and policy variants multiply.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run fleet-wide patch, rotation, backup and incident exercises.

tradeoffs.assessment: Requires tenant partition, identity routing, data move and key lifecycle tooling.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Canary one tenant with reversible export/import and dialog drain.

migrationNotes: Migrate one tenant at a time after active dialogs drain.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Route the tenant back to the shared service and restore the prior data/key binding.

opportunities.recommendation: Keep hardened Compose as the implemented local baseline and adopt orchestrated shards before multi-user production; use tenant cells only when isolation obligations justify their cost.

openQuestions: Peak calls per second, concurrent calls, codec mix, and regions?
Availability, recovery, retention, consent, deletion, and legal-hold requirements?
Are tenants mutually untrusted and do any require dedicated compute or keys?
Which external AI providers, if any, may receive audio or text?
